name: Sikasil Pool
paste:
SIKASIL® POOL: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikasil® Pool, September 2025, Version 04.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/1/sikasil_pool.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikasil® Pool where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2025, Version 04.01).
1.2 Product description. Sikasil® Pool is a 1-part, neutral curing silicone sealant for use in swimming pools and permanently wet areas.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Sikasil® Pool is used for sealing.
    - Areas under permanent water immersion
    - Wet areas between tiles, concrete, glass and metals
    - For interior and exterior use
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Please note.
    - The Product is not suitable for medical or pharmaceutical uses.
    - The Product cannot be overpainted.
    - The Product must not be used for joints with direct food contact.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikasil® Pool
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: SILICONE SEALANT FOR SWIMMING POOLS AND WET AREAS
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (September 2025, Version 04.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ISO 1183-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.1).
    - EN ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.2).
    - ISO 8339: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Secant tensile modulus (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN ISO 7389: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Elastic recovery (p.2).
    - EN ISO 9047: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - EN ISO 7390: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Sag flow (p.2).
    - CQP049-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Curing time (p.2).
    - CQP 019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Skinning time (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Good resistance to chlorinated water and common swimming pool cleaning chemicals
    - Movement capability of ± 25 %
    - Very good resistance to fungal attack
    - Neutral cure
    - Non-corrosive
    - High elasticity
    - High flexibility
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Neutral curing silicone
    - Colour: White, Grey, Transparent
    - Density: ~1.05 kg/L (ISO 1183-1)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: ~ 20 (after 28 days) (EN ISO 868)
    - Tensile strength: ~1.5 N/mm² (ISO 8339)
    - Secant tensile modulus: ~0.6 N/mm2 at 100 % elongation; (+23 °C) (ISO 8339)
    - Elastic recovery: > 90 % (EN ISO 7389)
    - Tear propagation resistance: ~4.0 N/mm (ISO 34-2)
    - Movement capability: ± 25 % (EN ISO 9047)
    - Service temperature: -40 °C min. / +80 °C max
2.7 Chemical resistance.
    - Good resistance to chlorinated water and common swimming pool cleaning chemicals
    The resistance of sealant to chlorine is dependent on the water pH value and the amount of free chlorine.
    Contact Sika Technical Services for additional information.
2.8 Joint design. The joint dimensions must be designed to suit the movement capability of the sealant. The joint width must be a minimum of 10 mm and a maximum of 35 mm. The joint depth must be a minimum of 6 mm and a maximum of 10 mm. For larger joints, contact Sika Technical Services for additional information.
2.9 Compatibility. Compatible with the following non-porous substrates:
    - Aluminium
    - Anodised aluminium
    - Stainless steel
    - Copper
    - Brass
    - Titanium- zinc
    - PVC
    - Galvanised steel
    - Powder and PVDF coated metals
    - Glazed tiles
    - Glass
    - Concrete
    - Unglazed tiles
    Compatible with the following porous substrates:
    For other substrate types, contact Sika Technical Services.
2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 15 months from date of production
2.11 Packaging.
    | 300 ml cartridge | 12 cartridges per box |
2.12 Storage conditions. The Product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +25 °C. Always refer to the packaging. Refer to the current Safety Data Sheet for information on safe handling and storage.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2025, Version 04.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation. Sikasil® Pool adheres without primers or activators. Poor adhesion due to inadequate surface preparation Note: Primers are adhesion promoters. Primers cannot replace proper surface preparation and surface cleaning. 1. Do not use primers for improving poorly prepared or poorly cleaned joint surfaces.
3.3 Non-porous substrates.
    - Aluminium, anodised aluminium, stainless steel, galvanised steel or glazed tiles 1. Lightly roughen the surface with a fine abrasive pad. 2. Clean the surface. 3. Pretreat the surface with Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth.
    - Other metals, such as copper, brass and titanium-zinc 1. Lightly roughen the surface with a fine abrasive pad. 2. Clean the surface. 3. Pretreat the surface with Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth. 4. Wait until the flash-off time is over. 5. Prime the surface with Sika® Primer-3 N applied with a brush.
    - PVC substrates 1. Prime the surface with Sika® Primer-215 applied with a brush.
    - Glass substrates 1. Clean the glass with Isopropanol before application.
3.4 Porous substrates.
    - Concrete and unglazed tiles 1. Prime the surface with Sika® Primer-3 N applied with a brush. 2. Wait until the flash-off time is over.
    - Before applying onto natural stone, contact Sika Technical Services.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2025, Version 04.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Backing material: Use closed cell, polyethylene foam backing rod.
    - Sag flow: < 2 mm (20 mm profile, +23 °C) (EN ISO 7390)
    - Curing time: ~2.0 mm / 24 hours (CQP049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~5 min (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
4.3 Consumption.
    | Joint width | Joint depth | Joint length per 300 ml |
    | cartridge |
    | 10 mm | 8 mm | 3.5 m |
    | 15 mm | 10 mm | 2 m |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.4 Important.
    - Degradation of sealant due to substrates leaching oil, plasticisers, or solvents
    - Bitumen, natural rubber or EPDM rubber can leach oils, plasticisers, or solvents that can degrade the sealant and cause the Product to become tacky. 1. Do not use the Product on building materials which leach oils, plasticisers, or solvents.
    - The substrate must be sound, clean, dry and free of contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, cement laitance, sealant residues and poorly bonded coatings which could affect adhesion of the primer and sealant.
    - The substrate must be of sufficient strength to handle the stress induced by the sealant during movement. 1. Use techniques such as wire brushing, grinding, grit blasting or other suitable mechanical methods to remove all weak substrate material. 2. Repair all damaged joint edges with suitable Sika repair products. 3. Remove dust, loose and friable material from all surfaces before applying the sealant.
    - Use the following priming or pre-treatment procedures to ensure optimum adhesion and joint durability:
4.5 Important. Poor adhesion due to incorrect priming procedure Incorrectly defined or uncontrolled priming procedures may lead to a variation in Product performance. 1. Test adhesion on project-specific substrates and agree on procedures with all parties before full project application. For more information contact Sika Technical Services.
4.6 Important.
    - Strictly follow installation procedures as defined in Method Statements, application manuals and working instructions which must always be adjusted to the actual site conditions.
    - Incorrect acid and base dosage increases the risk of fungal growth. 1. Use the Product in swimming pools and warm water whirlpools with a pH value between 6.5 and 7.6, and free chlorine < 5 mg/L (5 ppm). 2. Free available chlorine level must not be ≤ 0.3 mg/L in swimming pools and ≤ 0.7 mg/L in warm water whirlpools. 3. Maintain continuous water circulation to avoid chlorine concentrations. 4. Do not use acid-based detergents. 5. When joints must be reconstructed due to fungal growth, remove Sikasil® Pool completely beforehand. 1. Apply masking tape where neat or exact joint lines are required. 2. After the required substrate preparation, insert a backing rod to the required depth. 3. Prime the joint surfaces as recommended in substrate preparation. Note Avoid excessive application of the primer. 4. Fit the nozzle and cut it to the desired bead size. 5. Apply the Product into the joint. Note Avoid air entrapment. Make sure that the Product comes into full contact with the adhesion area of the joint. 6. IMPORTANT Do not use tooling products containing solvents. As soon as possible after application, tool the Product firmly against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion and a smooth finish. Use a compatible tooling agent such as Sika® Tooling Agent N to smooth the joint surface. 7. Remove the masking tape within the skin formation time of the Product.
    - Sikasil® Pool must be cured completely before filling the pool: minimum 7 days (depending on the temperature, humidity and thickness of sealant).
    - Colour variations
    - Note: Colour variations may occur due to the exposure in service to chemicals, high temperatures or UV-radiation (especially with white colour shade). This effect is aesthetic and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after use with Sika® Remover-208 or Sika® Cleaner- 350H. Once cured, hardened material can only be removed mechanically.
4.8 Further documentation - Refer to the following documents.
    - Pre-treatment chart for construction sealants and adhesives
    - Application manual - Joint Maintenance, Cleaning and Renovation

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.3 Dew point. The substrate temperature must be at least +3 °C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation decreasing adhesion.
5.4 Substrate temperature. +5 °C min. / +40 °C max.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: ~1.05 kg/L (ISO 1183-1)
    - Shore A hardness: ~ 20 (after 28 days) (EN ISO 868)
    - Tensile strength: ~1.5 N/mm² (ISO 8339)
    - Secant tensile modulus: ~0.6 N/mm2 at 100 % elongation; (+23 °C) (ISO 8339)
    - Elastic recovery: > 90 % (EN ISO 7389)
    - Tear propagation resistance: ~4.0 N/mm (ISO 34-2)
    - Movement capability: ± 25 % (EN ISO 9047)
    - Sag flow: < 2 mm (20 mm profile, +23 °C) (EN ISO 7390)
    - Curing time: ~2.0 mm / 24 hours (CQP049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~5 min (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikasil® Pool, September 2025, Version 04.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/1/sikasil_pool.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikasil®-Pool, version 18/06/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/v/sds-sikasil-pool.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
